questionText:
Consider the following pseudocode for depth-first search (DFS) algorithm which takes a directed graph $G(V, E)$ as input, where $d[v]$ and $f[v]$ are the discovery time and finishing time, respectively, of the vertex $v \in V$.

DFS(G):
  unmark all $v \in V$
  $t \leftarrow 0$
  for each $v \in V$
    if $v$ is unmarked
      $t \leftarrow Explore(G, v, t)$
    end if
  end for		Explore(G, v, t):
  mark $v$
  $t \leftarrow t + 1$
  $d[v] \leftarrow t$
  for each $(v, w) \in E$
    if $w$ is unmarked
      $t \leftarrow Explore(G, w, t)$
    end if
  end for
  $t \leftarrow t + 1$
  $f[v] \leftarrow t$
  return $t$


Suppose that the input directed graph $G(V, E)$ is a directed acyclic graph (DAG).

For an edge $(u, v) \in E$, which of the following options will NEVER be correct?
explanation:
Step 1: Understand the Parenthesis Theorem for DFS.
By the Parenthesis Theorem of DFS, for any pair of vertices $u$ and $v$, their discovery-finishing intervals $[d[u], f[u]]$ and $[d[v], f[v]]$ must either be completely disjoint or one must be strictly contained within the other.

Step 2: Analyze Option D.
Option D represents $d[u] < d[v] < f[u] < f[v]$, where the interval $[d[v], f[v]]$ overlaps with $[d[u], f[u]]$ without being fully nested. According to the Parenthesis Theorem, overlapping intervals are impossible in DFS for any graph. Therefore, Option D can NEVER be correct.

Step 3: Analyze Option B.
Option B represents $d[v] < d[u] < f[u] < f[v]$, which means $u$ is a descendant of $v$ in the DFS forest (i.e., there exists a path from $v$ to $u$). However, we are given that $(u, v) \in E$ is a directed edge from $u$ to $v$. If $u$ were a descendant of $v$, combining that path with the edge $(u, v)$ would form a directed cycle. Since $G$ is a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG), no directed cycle can exist. Thus, $u$ can never be a descendant of $v$, and Option B can NEVER be correct.

Step 4: Analyze Options A and C.
- Option A ($d[u] < d[v] < f[v] < f[u]$) occurs when $v$ is a descendant of $u$ (tree/forward edge), which is possible in a DAG.
- Option C ($d[v] < f[v] < d[u] < f[u]$) occurs when $v$ is visited and finished before $u$ is discovered (cross edge), which is also possible in a DAG.

Hence, options B and D will NEVER be correct.
